label: Bible Study
prompt: _____ and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
verse: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
note: Roots below, building above — Paul mixes a garden and a construction site.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the _____, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.
verse: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.
note: David's résumé for fighting Goliath: God saved me from the lion and the bear; He'll handle this one too.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small _____, whithersoever the governor listeth.
verse: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
note: Same lesson at sea: great ships driven by fierce winds still turn by a very small helm.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose _____ ye were healed.
verse: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.
note: Peter calls himself 'a witness of the sufferings of Christ' — here he hears Isaiah 53 in what he saw.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Speak ye _____ to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
verse: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
note: 'Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem' — literally 'speak to the heart.' Handel's Messiah opens with these very lines.
